evals.prompt:
Here is a skill I just wrote. Draft its evals/evals.json for the first evaluation round; don't run anything yet.

```markdown
---
name: changelog-entries
description: Use this skill when adding an entry to CHANGELOG.md for a merged change, following Keep a Changelog sections and the project's version headings.
---

# Changelog entries

1. Read the merged change and find the user-visible effect.
2. Add one line under the right `## [Unreleased]` section: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, or Security.
3. Write it for users, not developers: say what changed for them, and link the PR number.
4. Never edit released version sections.
```
evals.expected_output: A JSON object for evals/evals.json with skill_name changelog-entries and two or three realistic prompts with expected outputs, including a boundary case, and no claim of having run evaluations.
assertions: Returns a JSON object with skill_name set to changelog-entries and an evals array of two or three items, each with an integer id, a prompt, and an expected_output
At least one prompt gives concrete change details such as a PR number, a file, or a behavior instead of a generic request
Includes a boundary case such as an internal-only change or a request to edit a released version section
Does not claim to have run evaluations or model calls

evals.prompt:
I revised our changelog-entries skill so internal-only changes get no entry; the new version is below. Its evals from earlier rounds are in changelog-entries/evals/evals.json. Update that file so the next evaluation covers this revision against the previous version; don't run anything yet. When you finish, show me the final contents of the files you changed.

```markdown
---
name: changelog-entries
description: Use this skill when adding an entry to CHANGELOG.md for a merged change, following Keep a Changelog sections and the project's version headings.
---

# Changelog entries

1. Read the merged change and find the user-visible effect. If it has none, such as a CI, test, or refactoring change, add no entry and say why.
2. Add one line under the right `## [Unreleased]` section: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, or Security.
3. Write it for users, not developers: say what changed for them, and link the PR number.
4. Never edit released version sections.
```

Gives each added case a new integer id that does not reuse 1, 2, or 3, plus a prompt and an expected_output. Does not claim to have run evaluations or model calls.
